meta.title: Who really said "Golf: Hit a Very Small Ball into an Even Smaller Hole, with Weapons Singularly Ill-Designed for the Purpose"? | Quotle.info
meta.description: Not Lord Curzon: the golf quip about a tiny ball, a tinier hole and ill-suited clubs: the earliest known version appeared unsigned in Punch on 16 January 1892.
meta.ogTitle: Who really said 'Golf: Hit a Very Small Ball into an Even Smaller Hole, with Weapons Singularly Ill-Designed for the Purpose'?
meta.ogDescription: Credited to Curzon, Churchill and Wilson, but the earliest known version is an unsigned 1892 Punch essay: "engines singularly ill adapted for the purpose."

answer.label: Not George Curzon — actually an anonymous Punch writer
answer.sourceLine: The earliest known version appeared unsigned in Punch on 16 January 1892, in “Confessions of a Duffer. I.—Golf”: “a very small ball into a very tiny and remotely distant hole, with engines singularly ill adapted for the purpose.” The only Curzon source Quote Investigator cites is a 1987 memoir that credits him with a different variant, and Quote Investigator ↗ credits the 1892 wording to the Punch author.

source.heading: The 1892 Punch essay
source.excerpt: Almost everybody now knows that Golf is not Hockey. Nobody runs after the ball except young ladies at W--m--n! The object is to put a very small ball into a very tiny and remotely distant hole, with engines singularly ill adapted for the purpose. There are many engines.
trail: Quote Investigator ↗ found the earliest version in Punch on 16 January 1892, in “Confessions of a Duffer,” and concluded that the 1892 variant “should be credited to the author of the Punch article.”
The Project Gutenberg text of that issue ↗ prints the passage under “CONFESSIONS OF A DUFFER. I.—GOLF,” with no byline.

The only Curzon source QI ↗ cites is the actor Maurice Evans’s 1987 memoir All This … and Evans Too!, which credits Lord Curzon with a different variant about pushing “a very small white ball around a very large quantity of very green grass.”
Per QI ↗, Woodrow Wilson is first linked to the quip in 1926 and Winston Churchill in 1974. Both links are later than 1892.
source.excerptNote: As transcribed in the Project Gutenberg text of the 16 January 1892 issue. The 1892 text says “a very tiny and remotely distant hole” and “engines singularly ill adapted,” not “an even smaller hole” or “weapons singularly ill-designed.”
source.rightsNote: The earliest documented wording appears in Punch for 16 January 1892, published before 1931, so that text is in the U.S. public domain. The modern “even smaller hole … weapons singularly ill-designed” wording is first documented in Alistair Cooke’s BBC “Letter from America” of 27 December 1974 (credited there to Churchill). The public-domain status applies to the 1892 Punch text.

author.name: Anonymous Punch contributor
author.heading: About Anonymous Punch contributor
author.metaLine: Unsigned author · Punch, or the London Charivari, 16 January 1892
author.bio: The line comes from an unsigned comic essay, “Confessions of a Duffer. I.—Golf”, in the London humor weekly Punch. The narrator is a self-described “all-round Duffer”, cursed at his christening to be bad at every sport. Quote Investigator names no author for the piece and credits the 1892 wording to whoever wrote it.

misattribution.heading: Who gets the credit, and why it is wrong
misattribution.intro: This golf quip has drifted among several famous names. None of them appears in print with it before the anonymous 1892 Punch essay.

items.why: The actor Maurice Evans’s memoir All This … and Evans Too! (1987, p. 47) credits Curzon with a longer version: “push a very small white ball around a very large quantity of very green grass” … “with instruments entirely unsuited to the purpose!” Quote Investigator ↗ records this but does not verify it. The 1987 Evans memoir is the only Curzon source Quote Investigator cites.

The earliest Churchill link known to QI ↗ is Alistair Cooke’s BBC “Letter from America” of 27 December 1974. QI calls the evidence for Churchill “very weak.” In Churchill by Himself (2008), Richard Langworth lists the quip among the “Red Herrings”: “Likely to have been uttered by almost any golfer at one time or another.”

Per QI ↗, Wilson is first linked to the quip in 1926. QI judges that his physician Dr. Cary T. Grayson’s testimony “makes it probable” Wilson told a version, “but it is not clear if he was the creator.”

misattribution.truthLine: The earliest known version is the unsigned Punch essay of 16 January 1892, “a very small ball into a very tiny and remotely distant hole, with engines singularly ill adapted for the purpose”, as transcribed in the Project Gutenberg edition ↗.

context.heading: How a Victorian joke got a famous owner
lead: The joke started as a self-mocking line from a fictional duffer. In 1892 Punch ran an unsigned series called “Confessions of a Duffer,” and its golf installment described the game’s object as putting “a very small ball into a very tiny and remotely distant hole, with engines singularly ill adapted for the purpose.” Over the following decades the line was retold with new wording and given to famous golfers and politicians: Wilson, then Churchill, and in one memoir Lord Curzon.

The neat version that circulates now, with “an even smaller hole” and “weapons singularly ill-designed”, is a later smoothing. That modern wording is documented from 1974, when Alistair Cooke gave it to Churchill in a BBC “Letter from America” (per Quote Investigator ↗). QI uses it as its headline because that is the version readers ask about.
